verdict.reasoning: Transcript supports a 3‑day history and that the headache is 'really crazy' and 'probably an 8' in severity, but it does not say it is specifically 'worse today'; instead she notes it was worse the morning after onset and that it has been getting worse over three days.
Patient: 'It kind of feels all over my head, but like mainly around my right eye.' This supports mostly right periorbital with generalized component.
Patient: 'It's kind of. It's dull, but sometimes it gets a bit sharper. So basically it like it developed gradually...' explicitly matches dull ache, occasionally sharper, with gradual onset.

Patient: 'It kind of comes and goes, but I mean, it is there all the time, but like sometimes it's stronger.' and onset 'around three days ago' support persistence with fluctuating intensity and exacerbations over three days.
Doctor: 'how would you rate this headache?' Patient: 'It's probably an 8.' clearly supports 8/10 intensity.
Patient: 'I was thinking, okay, maybe I'll just go to sleep. Then I woke up the next morning like it was even, even worse, basically.' This supports the headache being worse after sleep.

Patient: 'So I tried ibuprofen. So I took like a few for the last two days, basically. But it doesn't really help.' and later clarifies 'Three a day.' This supports ibuprofen three times daily for two days being ineffective.
Patient: 'now like light is quite annoying my eyes.' Doctor: 'does it hurt to look at bright lights?' Patient: 'Yeah, yeah, it hurts.' This describes photophobia with eye pain in bright light.

Doctor: 'Have you had any loss of vision or blurry vision?' Patient: 'Not loss of vision, I wouldn't say. It's just like some lights from shooting light speed.' This supports denial of loss/blurry vision and presence of 'shooting lights.'

Doctor: 'Any nausea or any vomiting?' Patient: 'Well, basically I'm sick with the headache, but I. No vomiting.' Feeling 'sick' with no vomiting is a reasonable description of mild nausea without vomiting.

Doctor sequentially asks about 'Any neck pain or neck stiffness?', 'any difficulty with speaking or speech?', 'Any difficulty with weakness in your arms and legs?', 'Any temperatures or fevers?', 'Any rashes at all on your skin?' and the patient answers 'No' to each. This supports denial of fever, neck stiffness, rash, speech difficulty, and limb weakness.
Patient: 'It's hard to focus though, so I had to take a couple of days off work actually.' supports difficulty concentrating and days off work.
Patient: 'Yeah, I mean, I had, but usually after I take ibuprofen, it kind of goes away, so. But this time it's just not.' This indicates prior similar headaches responsive to ibuprofen.

Patient: 'I'm like worried. I don't want it to be a migraine... And I know it's genetic, so I've researched that, but I don't know if that is the case.' This supports concern about migraine and research into genetics; triggers are not explicitly mentioned, but migraine concern and genetics research are.
Doctor: 'Do you have any other medical history?' Patient: 'I think so. It's just a headache.' implies no other past medical history volunteered.
Doctor: 'do you take any regular medication?' Patient: 'No.' directly supports no regular medications.
Patient: 'So I tried ibuprofen... I took like a few for the last two days, basically.' and later 'Three a day.' supports ibuprofen three times daily over the past two days.
Doctor: 'Do you have any allergies to any medications?' Patient: 'Not that I know of.' supports no known drug allergies.
Patient: 'my sister and my mum have them quite frequently.' about migraines, and doctor reiterates 'your mother and sister both have migraines.' confirming family history.
Doctor: 'Who lives at home with you?' Patient: 'I live with housemates, so three of them.' supports living with three housemates.

Patient: 'I work in it, so I work with computers a lot, so it kind of is difficult to focus. I had to like reduce the brightness of my screen.' While she does not explicitly say 'aggravates the headache,' needing to reduce brightness due to difficulty focusing in context of headache implies screen use worsens symptoms.

Doctor: 'Do you wear glasses?' Patient: 'Yes, I do.' Doctor: 'Have you had a recent eye check done? Eye test?' Patient: 'No, I've been wearing them since I was five.' supports glasses use and no recent eye check.
Doctor: 'Regarding smoking or alcohol, do you drink or smoke at all?' Patient: 'I socially smoke...' supports social smoking.
Patient: 'I socially smoke and I drink. Not only socially.' This contradicts 'drinks alcohol socially'; she explicitly says drinking is not only social.

Doctor: 'Have you been feeling more stressed or anxious at work? Recently?' Patient: 'Well, it's been a bit stressful kicking off a new project, but yeah, nothing out of the ordinary really.' supports some recent stress but no severe anxiety.

Doctor: 'I do think this could be a headache very similar to migraine... The history is very suggestive of it.' in context of an 8/10, persistent, worsening headache supports assessment of acute severe headache with possible migraine.

Transcript documents 3‑day duration, right‑sided/periorbital distribution, photophobia ('hurts to look at bright lights'), feeling 'sick' without vomiting, family history of migraine, and poor response to ibuprofen, matching the summarized assessment.
Doctor: 'You can take up to two tablets three times a day.' given in response to ibuprofen use supports discussion of correct dosing up to 2 tablets TID.

Doctor: 'I can prescribe you something stronger like naproxen... We can also add in other painkillers like paracetamol or codeine... I can give you a prescription for that today.' supports offering naproxen and codeine prescriptions.
Doctor: 'We can also add in other painkillers like paracetamol or codeine, which might be helpful as well.' explicitly discusses paracetamol as an option.
Doctor: 'it may be worth keeping a headache diary so we can try and work out what's. If there's any triggers...' supports advice to keep a headache diary.

Doctor: 'I'd like you to come back and see me in about a week's time. Week to two weeks time. If you are having more frequent episodes... we can think about giving you medications as prophylactic...' supports 1–2 week follow‑up with possible migraine prophylaxis if recurrent.

Doctor: 'If your headaches aren't getting any better or they're getting worse... If you have any problems with your vision or weakness in your arms and legs, or you're just not feeling very well, just give me a call and come back and see me.' This educates about warning signs (vision changes, neurological deficits, systemic unwellness) and seeking care.
Doctor: 'if you feel like your eyes are straining, I would always recommend having a repeat eye test done.' supports advice to have an eye test if eye strain persists.
Doctor: 'I'd like you to come back and see me in about a week's time. Week to two weeks time.' clearly sets 1–2 week follow‑up.
The transcript includes only history and counseling; there is no mention of physical examination or vital signs. Stating that no exam/vitals were documented matches this absence.
Patient: 'now like light is quite annoying my eyes.' and 'Yeah, yeah, it hurts.' to bright lights is consistent with photophobia.
Patient: 'when it started I got this like weird shooting lights...' and later 'some lights from shooting light speed.' supports occasional 'shooting lights' in vision.
Patient: 'Well, basically I'm sick with the headache, but I. No vomiting.' supports mild nausea (feeling sick) without vomiting.
As in hpi-010, the patient answers 'No' to questions about fever, neck pain/stiffness, rash, speech difficulty, and limb weakness, supporting these denials.
